subject: Measurement invariance not constraining residuals across groups

messages.author: 88cc50a7df20ac58
messages.subject: Measurement invariance not constraining residuals across groups
parts:
As similar to a previous conversation: "Measurement Invariance group.equal not constraining residuals"

I am also having a similar issue but I have used measeq.syntax, parameterisation theta, and constrained the thresholds. I won't write out my model, but it is a 9 correlated factor model.

scale←measEq.syntax(configural=Corfactor, data=data,

parameterization = “theta”, group = “Reporter”,

ordered=T, std.lv=T,

group.equal=c(“loadings”, “thresholds”),

meanstructure =T)

scale<as.character(scale)

fit.scale←cfa(scale, data=data, group = “Reporter”, estimator=”WLSMV”, ordered=T)


strict←measEq.syntax(configural=Corfactor, data=data,

parameterization = “theta”, group = “Reporter”,

ordered=T, std.lv=T,

group.equal=c(“loadings”, “thresholds”, “residuals”),

meanstructure =T)

strict<as.character(strict)

fit.strict←cfa(strict, data=data, group = “Reporter”, estimator=”WLSMV”, ordered=T)


These models are very similar, with a slight increase in the degrees of freedom of the strict model, and the residuals don't appear to have been constrained. The names of the residual parameters are the same across the groups but the values are different.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance not constraining residuals across groups
parts: fit.strict←cfa(strict, data=data, group = “Reporter”, estimator=”WLSMV”, ordered=T)

The names of the residual parameters are the same across the groups but the values are different.


You chose parameterization = "theta" when you generated your syntax, but not when you fit that model to the data.
